_comment: Outbound trunk — needed to DIAL A REP for the warm transfer.
The inbound trunk answers carriers; this one places the call to the rep so
they can be briefed before the carrier is joined to them.
lk sip outbound create sip_setup/outbound-trunk.json
Then put the id it prints (ST_...) into .env as LIVEKIT_SIP_OUTBOUND_TRUNK_ID.
The LiveKit dashboard's Telephony -> Create a new trunk -> Outbound form is the
same thing if you'd rather click; auth_username / auth_password live under its
'Optional settings' section.
LiveKit does not carry calls to the PSTN — it is the SIP client. `address` is
always a CARRIER's SIP host, so a rep's phone is reached through whoever
terminates your calls (the same Twilio trunk that handles inbound, or another
provider). Fields:
address        the carrier's SIP termination host, NO 'sip:' prefix and no
trailing path. Twilio: <your-trunk>.pstn.twilio.com
transport      AUTO unless your carrier requires one. TLS if you want the
signalling encrypted and the carrier supports it.
numbers        the caller ID the REP sees. Must be a number you own on that
trunk, E.164. Use the main brokerage line so it looks familiar.
auth_username  the carrier's termination credentials. Twilio: a Credential
auth_password  List attached to the trunk. Some carriers use an IP allow-list
instead, in which case leave these out and whitelist LiveKit.
Never commit real credentials: fill these in a local copy.
